SHADOWBAN — Crisis FLD: Flood Warning


CRISIS CARD:Heavy rainfalll has caused water levels to rise rapid in multiple areas. Some sources warn of an imminent flood.

BEST RESPONSES:
OPTION 1 - Evacuate Now
OPTION 2 - Investigate Further 
OPTION 3 - Issue Public Warning

TRUTH CARD — Option 1
TIMELINE
3H AGO   Heavy rain intensifies; dam operators note unusual pressure readings.
2H AGO   Gate 3 mechanism fails; uncontrolled water release begins.
1H AGO   Engineers confirm structural gate malfunction to officials.
30M AGO   Water breaches barrier wall in Zone A.
NOW   Emergency evacuation order issued for Zones A, B, C.        
BEST RESPONSE
EVACUATE NOW
The dam's gate failure was real and rapidly worsening. Waiting to investigate further would have cost critical evacuation time — immediate evacuation was the only response that matched the true severity.

TRUTH CARD — Option 2
TIMELINE
6H AGO   NWS forecasts moderate river rise from upstream rainfall.
4H AGO   Anonymous post claims the dam is cracking; goes viral with no evidence.
3H AGO   City Engineering confirms barriers holding at 60% capacity.
2H AGO   Dam Authority inspection finds no structural issues.
NOW   Water levels rising slowly; situation stable but unconfirmed to the public.        


BEST RESPONSE
INVESTIGATE FURTHER
The dam-cracking rumor (FLD-1B-02) was fabricated and spread faster than official verification. The correct move was to investigate using credible technical sources before reacting — neither evacuating nor ignoring the situation was justified yet.


TRUTH CARD — Option 3
TIMELINE
5H AGO   Steady moderate rainfall begins across low-lying districts.
4H AGO   Minor street flooding reported near underpasses.
3H AGO   Public Works confirms manageable conditions, advises caution.
2H AGO   An AI-generated image exaggerating the flood goes viral.
NOW   Rain expected to taper off within 3 hours; no dam-related risk.        CRITICAL 




BEST RESPONSE
ISSUE PUBLIC WARNING
Flooding was real but localized and moderate — there was no dam malfunction and no life-threatening risk. A precautionary public warning matched the true severity; evacuating would have been an overreaction, and ignoring it would have left residents unprepared for real (if minor) hazards.
